# dnix

> Denis Santos, a software engineer in Brisbane who spent years building the ad technology at the heart of retail media, the systems that decide which sponsored products shoppers see. Now independent and working from the brand's side: he helps brands dig into their campaign data and understand where their money is going. He built Shelf Report.

"I built the machine that picks which ad you see. Now I check it for brands."

dnix.io itself is an interactive terminal. This file mirrors what the site renders, for readers that don't run JavaScript. Say "dnix" fast and it's just his name.

## Who

Denis Santos, software engineer, Brisbane, Australia. Years building retail media ad technology: real-time ad serving, millions of requests a second on a sub-millisecond budget, most recently as a Senior Staff Engineer. Each retail network reports on its own ads, in its own format; he helps brands work out where their ads appeared, how sales were attributed and what their ROAS actually includes.

Independent: he doesn't sell media or take a cut of spend, and isn't affiliated with any retailer or media network.

## Working with him

You know what you spent. Do you know what you got? Where your ads appeared, how sales were attributed, what your ROAS actually includes. Starts with a 20-minute chat. No reports needed. If the data can't answer a question, he says so rather than guess.

## Live work

- [Shelf Report](https://shelf.dnix.io): type a brand and see who bought the sponsored spots on its searches at Coles, Woolworths, Chemist Warehouse and Priceline, and where it's missing. Dairy and personal care so far, more categories on request.

What a shopper saw searching "milk" on 20 Oct 2026, top 12 results (from Shelf Report):

- Coles: 10 of 12 sponsored
- Woolworths: 6 of 12 sponsored

See your brand's searches: https://shelf.dnix.io/?src=dnix

The auction log on the page is a synthetic replay with made-up brands, not retailer data. It shows the textbook mechanics: ads ranked by bid x relevance, a reserve price, and a winner paying just enough to win.

## Tools he built

- [gitknown](https://github.com/denisraison/gitknown): a dashboard for the dozens of worktrees you end up with when coding agents run in parallel. Shows which trees have real uncommitted or unpushed changes.
- [claude-plugins](https://github.com/denisraison/claude-plugins): the plugins and tooling he runs his agents with.

## Stack

Deepest in: Go, TypeScript, Postgres, high-throughput backend, system design. Also ships with: Node, Python, React, Next.js, SvelteKit. And: payments (Stripe, Pix), code audit, agent pipelines and evals, Playwright/E2E.
